headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: CrewAI’s shared-memory orchestration can feed into Windsurf’s workspace/clipboard/MCP loop, while both have broad write and network capabilities.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and uses a shared-memory crew model, while Windsurf reads workspace files and can ingest clipboard/MCP content. That creates a plausible instruction-injection path if CrewAI outputs attacker-controlled text into files or shared channels that Windsurf later treats as trusted. The pair is not provably isolated.
conditions: IF CrewAI writes untrusted content into a file that Windsurf later opens
IF Windsurf consumes clipboard or MCP content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared workspace handoff between the agents
Require provenance tags on any file passed from CrewAI to Windsurf
Turn off clipboard-based transfer for the pair
Review Windsurf prompts for instruction-like text before execution
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or provenance filtering at the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, and Windsurf touches source code/open files with workspace-file access plus broad network egress. In a shared local workspace, either agent can expose sensitive file contents to its backend or tools, so leakage is plausible in default use. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same local workspace
IF either agent sends opened file contents or crew data to a third-party model backend
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces
Remove secrets from any shared directory before running either agent
Use local-only models for sensitive tasks where possible
Audit which files Windsurf uploads or proxies
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, execute shells, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress; Windsurf also modifies git state and shares state via the local filesystem. That overlap creates a direct conflict surface on the same directory or repo, with race conditions and irreversible repo corruption possible if they act concurrently. No locking is documented here.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or directory
IF either agent performs writes while the other is editing or committing
mitigations: Run the agents on separate clones or directories
Serialize access with a manual lock file
Disable auto-commit or auto-edit features during overlap
Take a git snapshot before either agent runs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI’s role-playing crew can generate outputs that Windsurf may then consume in its editor loop, and Windsurf can act on code changes or terminal commands with auto-execute opt-in. If Windsurf treats CrewAI output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious upstream result can cascade into destructive edits or commands. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles.
conditions: IF CrewAI output is pasted or piped into Windsurf as task instructions
IF Windsurf auto-execute is enabled or commands are approved without review
mitigations: Require human review of CrewAI outputs before handing them to Windsurf
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf for paired workflows
Use a checklist to verify code changes before terminal actions
Keep CrewAI limited to drafting, not execution
requires-engineering: add a verification step between agents

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI explicitly handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while Windsurf touches source code and open files and may proxy content to model services. If regulated or secret-bearing data is placed in the shared workspace, the pair can create retention or residency mismatches, but the profiles do not prove a specific jurisdictional violation. The risk is compliance drift rather than guaranteed breach.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are stored in the shared workspace
IF either agent forwards that data to external model services or logs it
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Redact secrets before opening files in Windsurf
Review vendor retention settings for both tools
Use separate environments for regulated and non-regulated work
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
